free_tier.stated: 32 GiB maximum per project, and at most 10 unpublished projects per user. Both are config knobs (process.max_upload_size, services.upload_limit) rather than business limits, and they differ per deployment. Publishing requires at least one successfully parsed entry, and publishing is what frees the 10-project slot.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous for published entries via the NOMAD API and GUI.

tooling: Documented REST API requires HTTP authentication tokens for uploads via API endpoints. File parsers are plugin-based and format validation depends on target deployment configuration.
chaining: 10 unpublished projects × 32 GiB = 320 GiB of live scratch on a free account, and publishing an entry releases a slot. So the steady-state ceiling is bounded by how fast a human can publish, not by bytes.
limits_note: fails-quota at 32 GiB, and write-gated by the parser: 'A project must contain at least one successfully processed entry before it can be published.' Content must be materials-science-shaped (DFT codes, ELN exports) to be parseable at all. Both limits together make it useless as bulk storage despite the clean API.
reliability_note: Well-run EU (FAIRmat) infrastructure with a real API. The constraint is semantic, not technical.

extras.tooling_verbatim: A documented REST API (I got HTTP 401 'Authentication required.' from /prod/v1/api/v1/info, which is the correct behaviour — a real auth gate, not a fake 200) with API-token upload from the GUI's 'Upload via API' dialog. extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.

binding_note: no constraint of a named kind was recorded; the verdict rests on the quota sentence rather than on a named limit
